newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends losses at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended losses at the close as buyers, either well covered or discouraged by recent strengthening of the ringgit against the dollar, stayed at the sidelines, dealers said.

"There has not been many inquiries since the beginning of the year. And we don't expect buyers to return so soon," said a Malaysian dealer. She said most consumers were well covered with some having bought up to April/May positions.
Dealers said though prices have been on the downtrend, they need to come off further in order to weather off competition from cheaper rubber in Thailand and Indonesia.

But further downside could be limited as producers were unlikely to sell at much lower prices, dealers said. "There were already not many sellers at current levels. I don't think prices can come down very much from here," said another dealer.

Dealers said the twin festivals of Chinese Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr next month, when plantations stop tapping rubber for nearly a week, should not have much effect on supply as stocks were at a comfortable level due to lack of demand.
Feb RSS1 buyer and SMR 20 buyer were quoted at 302 ($1.21) and 297 cents ($1.19) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, both down 1.50 cents from Thursday.
